title: When the Phone Takes the Whole Evening: Help Your Teen Take It Back Without Confiscating It
summary: Agree on a teen-designed start to the evening while keeping adult-owned sleep, safety, and shared-household limits; review it together instead of repeating nightly phone fights.
seo_title: Teen on Phone All Evening? What Works
seo_description: Teen on phone all evening? Agree on a first half-hour they design, keep clear sleep and family limits, then review together instead of fighting every night.
release_move: The parent keeps sleep, safety, and shared-household boundaries while the teen designs and tries the evening start and reviews it once a week.

core_belief_shift.from: If I do not take the phone away every night, nothing will change.
core_belief_shift.to: We can try a teen-designed start to the evening and review it weekly while I keep necessary sleep and safety limits.

book_relevance.reason: The live Discipline Playbook names a phone or video taking the whole evening; its teen-owned first-action practice complements the parent's independent evening plan. The article must remain useful without this bridge.

next_step.label: Help your teen start a specific task
next_step.reason: Once the evening has a start, use this for a separate schoolwork starting barrier.

hero.alt: A teenager puts her phone aside on a hallway shelf and opens her school bag while her father folds laundry in the next room.

social_image.alt: A teen chooses a small evening start after setting her phone down, while her father gives her space in the next room.
